skill.description: Use the inference.sh CLI to discover, run, and monitor cloud AI apps for media, LLM, search, and automation workflows.
skill.summary: Run inference.sh AI apps from an agent-friendly CLI workflow.
skill.author: skillssh

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms critical remote-installer guidance that pipes downloaded content directly into a shell. Most API-key, documentation-link, shell-completion, and Markdown backtick findings are false positives, but the skill still performs real external CLI work. No prompt injection evidence was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell installation with explicit download, checksum verification, signature verification, and a separate user-run install command.

remediation.issue: Manual install uses shell command substitution to select a remote artifact.
remediation.suggestion: Provide stable per-platform download links or package-manager commands, and avoid parsing remote metadata inside shell substitutions.

remediation.issue: Local file paths are automatically uploaded to cloud apps.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before uploading local files and document how users can review paths before execution.

remediation.issue: Twitter/X commands can change account state.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval for posts, media uploads, follows, likes, retweets, and direct messages.

content.user_title: Run AI Apps with the inference.sh CLI
content.value_statement: Teams need one interface for many hosted AI models and media tools. This skill helps agents discover, run, and monitor inference.sh apps from the CLI.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation, login, and API key setup for the infsh CLI.
Lists, searches, filters, and inspects available inference.sh apps.
Runs apps with inline inputs, saved input files, and version-pinned app names.
Supports long-running jobs with no-wait submission and task status checks.
Uses local file paths for supported media upload workflows.
Covers image, video, LLM, search, 3D, utility, and Twitter/X app categories.
limitations: Requires the infsh CLI, an inference.sh account, and valid credentials.
Requests, prompts, and selected files may be sent to cloud services.
Results depend on app schemas, account credits, provider availability, and permissions.
Twitter/X actions require connected credentials and explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Prototype AI Workflows
use_cases.description: Find available models, inspect input schemas, run sample jobs, and compare results before integrating an API.

use_cases.title: Create Media Assets
use_cases.description: Generate images, videos, avatars, audio, and 3D assets from prompts or approved local source files.

use_cases.title: Operate Hosted AI Jobs
use_cases.description: Submit long-running jobs, track task status, save outputs, and coordinate repeatable CLI-based AI operations.

prompt_templates.title: Find an App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to find image generation apps for realistic product photos. Show the best options and explain required inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Simple Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to run a text-to-image job for a clean product mockup. Confirm the app and input before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Track a Long Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to start a video generation job without waiting. Then check the task status and summarize the result.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Model Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use infsh-cli to compare three LLM or search apps for a research workflow. Include schema differences, strengths, and limits.

output_examples.input: Find a strong image app for product photography.
output: Recommended FLUX and Gemini image apps with short reasons.
Listed the main input fields needed for each app.
Suggested generating a sample input before running a paid job.

output_examples.input: Run a long video job and check it later.
output: Selected a video app and confirmed the prompt with the user.
Submitted the job in no-wait mode.
Returned the task identifier and later summarized the completed result.

output_examples.input: Use a local image as source media.
output: Confirmed the exact local file path before upload.
Explained that the file would be sent to a cloud app.
Reported the returned media link after the task completed.

best_practices: Inspect app schemas before running jobs with complex inputs.
Confirm every local file path before upload to a cloud app.
Use no-wait mode for long media jobs and track task status separately.
anti_patterns: Do not run installer commands without verifying the source and checksum.
Do not upload broad directories or sensitive local files by default.
Do not post, follow, like, retweet, or send messages without explicit approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents use the infsh CLI to discover, run, and monitor hosted AI apps.

faq.question: Does it require an account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need an inference.sh account and either CLI login or an INFSH_API_KEY value.

faq.question: Can it generate images and videos?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include image, video, avatar, audio, 3D, and utility app examples.

faq.question: Can it use local files?
faq.answer: Yes. Supported apps can accept local file paths, which the CLI uploads to the cloud.

faq.question: Can it automate Twitter or X?
faq.answer: Yes, but account actions should require explicit user approval before execution.

faq.question: Is it safe to install automatically?
faq.answer: The audit flagged pipe-to-shell installer guidance. Users should verify downloads and signatures before installation.
